The Speaker of Contemplation looked at the ragged mass of flora before her, lost and without purpose. The Flora, once mighty, have fallen far. With shattered pride, and now being forced to flee their homeland, they would a new purpose to unite and to define them. This was what Sentenza was for, it was a city made by and for those who had lost everything, and to give them a chance to dream once more.

She saw Mar'dy will the Flora to action, but Mar'dy was foolish, the Flora's strength were never on the fields of battle, it was with their minds and machines that they conducted warfare. Those who fought would be needed, but there would also be need for the Flora's other talents.

*"My brethren, poor flora, I am sorry I could not give you a warm welcome to our fair city. I can only make of you an offer, and a request."*

*"As we speak, harbingers of your destruction arrive from over the horizon, and I can only promise you that every free Spectre, every citizen of Sentenza will defend all those who inhabit it to their dying breath. This extends to you, and we must ask of your assistance. The flora are renowned for their machinery and intelligence, your understanding is unparalleled in all races, and so we humbly ask for your assistance."*

"*Join us in the fight for the right to live, free from the stifling tyranny of those who wish to take everything from us. You wish to spread the pattern? Help us to carve the divine pattern into the bodies of our foes. You wish to die for a great cause, then die fighting, for the right to live free. All we ask of you, is to man our catapults, calculate the trajectories of our launch, and fire these crystals, carriers of the divine pattern, into the heart of those who would have you destroyed."*

*"All we ask, is that you prove that you deserve the right to live. To live is to suffer, to bear hardship and understand the consequences. To live is to stumble and rise again. The flora have fallen, this is known to all on Gaea. Prove yourselves here, on the fields of battle, and we will help you to your feet. Rise from the ashes of the past, take with you the mistakes of yesterday. The flora have allowed themselves to become puppets. Never again shall you be enslaved! The Flora have accepted their fall, only to be hunted at their darkest hour. Never again will you bear to suffer in silence."*

*"We will help you with the means to leave the mark, we will help you get back your freedom, but we need your help. All you need to do, is speak, and we will broadcast your voice across the land. Your response will be made in the wreckage of your foes, in the destruction of the land on which they tread. What say you, that we mark this a new beginning, forged on the fields of battle in the fight for your right to live."*

The flora sat, silent, staring blankly. Then one stood up, voice quivering, and the Speaker knew his question even before it was asked.

"Why?"

*"For we believe every race has the right to choose their own destiny, to forge their own future. The fate of the flora has always been decided for them. Not here, not now. If you gaze into the crystal tower, you will see that the future itself is uncertain. There is no certainty after this point, no clear outcome on the other side of the battle. This is a chance for the races of Gaea to finally stand up and fight, even if the odds are insurmountable, even if it is beyond all hope. We ask for your aid because we require it, and also because you require it. Throughout your history, you have been made to be pawns, and punished for actions that were not your fault. For your kind to rise again, to become even a shadow of what you once were, you will have to take matters into your own hands. Even if the world is against you, you must fight. In order to be sure of victory, you must fight. Every moment of every day, you must fight, sometimes invaders, sometimes yourselves. The Lord of Order does not see the necessity of this conflict. This struggle gives life its meaning, this struggle gives us despair, but it also gives us hope. In every destruction there lies the hope for creation, every ending the chance for a new beginning."*

*"We think you deserve the chance, to begin again."*

Cruxius watched the battle unfold eagerly. It was all so exciting he even forgot to keep counting.

These Flora, however, were of no use to him, or Sentenza, slaves as they were to obsession. He heard a single Flora speak up: "Why?" it asked. Cruxius echoed this back into the minds of all the Flora in Sentenza. A million times, in a million voices, "Why?"

And they snapped. No longer did they have the resolve to draw these pointless patterns. They had once been a strong, powerful race, with great machines and advancements to help the people of Gaea, and yet here they stood, ages apart from their former glory, with a singular purpose. A purpose, that was now marred by uncertainty and disdain.

A single voice this time rang out to them. A gentle breeze. It promised strength. Conviction. Drive. Certainty. Purpose, and behind that voice another spoke of freedom. As one the Flora of Sentenza sloughed off their shackles of obsession and embraced the uncertainty of their future. And, for the first time in ages long past, the Flora lived again as free creatures.
